about: Vocabulary of record for the Gaia Skill Tree HQ. States: canonical (use this), banned (already retired by CONTEXT.md — CI fails), parked (coined but unchosen — internal docs only, never user-facing copy or code), frozen (meant something specific once — archived docs only). A term is `banned` ONLY when CONTEXT.md's `## Banned synonyms` section already retired it; a term this repo is still arguing about is `parked`, never banned. Writing a linter is not a way to make a decision — CONTEXT.md decides, this gate enforces.
namespace_note: THE LEXICON IS FEDERATED ACROSS TWO HQs (ratified V5-8). This repo owns gaia.skills and gaia.trust. gaia-research/gaia-research owns core, gaia.research, gaia.brand, gaia.heaven and gaia.mcp. skill-heaven and gaia-mcp own NO namespace — they consume. `gaia.registry` is REJECTED: the namespace is `gaia.skills`, the same ruling as #1258 ("Gaia Registry" is not the product name). ONE TERM, ONE OWNER: a term is defined in exactly one file, ever. This root file carries the repo-wide config AND the `gaia.skills` namespace's own terms; `gaia.trust` is a peer under `core` in scripts/lexicon/lexicon.gaia.trust.json. The 54 terms the other HQ owns are mirrored NAME-ONLY into scripts/lexicon/lexicon.foreign.json, so this gate can reject a redefinition without importing another repo's source.
path_note: The JSON lives under scripts/lexicon/ rather than founder/ because branch-scope CI only lets an `infra/*` branch touch .github/, scripts/, *.md and docs/*.html — and this gate is infra. The generated founder/LEXICON.md is a *.md file, so it sits where a reader expects it. The checker resolves its root from either location, which is what lets scripts/lexicon/check-lexicon.ts stay byte-identical to the copy in gaia-research.
oracle_note: `oracle` is null because this HQ has no RATIFICATION.md-style decision table. CONTEXT.md's `## Banned synonyms` section is the oracle of record here, cited in prose on each banned term. CONTEXT.md itself is excluded from the scan: it is the supersession log, so it must be able to name a retired word without failing the gate that retired it.
scope_note: THE GATE IS SURFACE-SCOPED, NOT REPO-SCOPED. It reads .md and .ts under the scopes below. registry/, registry-for-review/, skill-trees/, docs/graph/ and generated-output/ are excluded: they are data and generated artifacts, curated through `gaia dev` verbs, and a vocabulary linter has no business rewriting a contributor's skill description.

decisive.about: Docs that read as current guidance: agent contracts, founder docs, the repo's own instructions.

user-facing.about: Copy a reader outside the project sees.

code.about: Shipped source. Parked vocabulary must never become an identifier.

terms.definition: The product name, in headline, title and OG copy. The org is Gaia Research; "the registry" (lower-case, no Gaia prefix) is the data-layer term only.
Retired as a product name / proper noun. The same ruling names the v5 namespace `gaia.skills` rather than `gaia.registry`.
terms.note: The lower-case descriptive "the registry" is still correct for the data layer; only the capitalised proper-noun form is retired.

terms.definition: A skill with a contributor-authored implementation in `registry/named/`, as opposed to a generic skill, which is a catalogue entry with no implementation attached.
A catalogue node in `registry/nodes/` describing a capability with no contributor implementation attached. Its named forms are separate terms.
The structural type (`type=fusion`) for a skill composed from prerequisites. Stands bare — the "Skill" suffix is a rank-word convention, not a type-word one.
Legacy Yggdrasil I taxonomy word for the composed type, along with `type=extra`.
Retired tier synonym for the uncomposed type.
Retired synonym for the 5★ rank name.
Retired synonym for the 5★ rank name. Scoped to copy and code: it is a word an internal note may legitimately quote while explaining why it is gone.

Where a user's skill level actually lives. Levels are stored in slots on `skill-trees/<user>/skill-tree.json`, never on the skill object — anything computing stats, trees or breakdowns must read the slot.
